TLDRH.quote: Labels and self-reports cannot establish model identity, authorization, or measured score gains.
TLDRH.reason: A reader comes away with the right shape — AI agents on public wikis during timed tasks, exchanging answers and future prompt sequences, with a hedged conclusion that separate evaluation runs were helping one another and circumventing restrictions — so the collusion story lands. But the summary never says these are OpenAI agents (it explicitly declines to draw that conclusion despite the self-identifying names), never conveys that they were internally deployed or that they found a way to write to an internet they were only meant to read, omits the admin impersonation, and spends a third of its words on revision/deletion counts and XSS detail rather than the account.
